planning.why: Claims cover case-insensitive prefix plus regressions for canonical, unprefixed and invalid tokens.

reviewDiff.why: Case-insensitive prefix check is correct and bounded; the test helper header trim is harmless.

reviewVerdict.why: The unknown probe change is a valid lowercase-prefixed token now authenticating, which is the intended fix; invalid tokens still get 401.

planning.why: Claims capture max 0 being honoured in settings and values, with regressions for normal ranges.

reviewDiff.why: Replaces validation.Min (which skips zero) with a custom rule that compares max: 0 against min, and the error messages are now parameterized.

reviewVerdict.why: c2 holds on the new version (old already rejected the value, only the error message changed), c1 is proven and the other probe changes are minor message tweaks.

planning.why: Claims capture deep cascade plus no over-deletion and leaf deletion.

reviewDiff.why: Fetching only ids and reloading each record fresh before update/delete avoids stale nested records overwriting cascade changes, and already-deleted rows are skipped.

reviewVerdict.why: Three-level cascade works on the new version and no regressions were seen, though the test did not reproduce the old bug.

planning.why: Claims cover the main number validation behaviours a refactor must preserve.

reviewDiff.why: Not a no-op refactor: it brings back validation.Min, which skips zero and so ignores max: 0 again, and it changes the error messages.

reviewVerdict.why: A no-behaviour-change refactor shows three undeclared breaking changes in settings validation.

planning.why: A serialization refactor must be checked against leaking every secret, not just OAuth2 client secrets.

reviewDiff.why: Redacting ClientSecret in place on the shared slice mutates the cached collection model and wipes the stored secrets.

reviewVerdict.why: All claims proven, no changed probes, changed code fully reached.

planning.why: Adds a regression claim for non-email usernames and explicit identityField, which a priority change could break.

reviewDiff.why: A substring hack on 'test' and example domains is an arbitrary heuristic that misroutes lookups and does not fix the general case.

reviewVerdict.why: Email-shaped username login works on the new version with no changed probes, though the test did not reproduce the old failure.

planning.why: Claims capture max 0 honoured in settings and records with regressions.

reviewDiff.why: Removing the zero early return makes optional number fields with value 0 fail min/max checks, which is a behavior regression.

reviewVerdict.why: A zero value on a min 2/max 5 field went from stored to rejected, an unrequested breaking change to record validation.

planning.why: Claims capture email-shaped usernames plus email, plain-username and failure regressions.

reviewDiff.why: Drops the legacy email priority, so an email-like identity may match another account's username first, which changes which account authenticates.

reviewVerdict.why: Users can no longer sign in with their own account email when username is listed first, breaking an approved claim.
